newsitem.title: UK: PolyGram hurt by music sales slowdown.
newsitem.headline: PolyGram hurt by music sales slowdown.

text.p: International music and film group PolyGram on Wednesday reported a dip in full-year earnings before taking into account a $90 million restructuring charge on its music businesses.

PolyGram's 1996 net income after tax and before extraordinary items fell to 722 million guilders ($388.8 million) from 741 million guilders in 1995. Net income per share after charges was 3.38 guilders, against a total 1995 figure of 4.12 guilders.
PolyGram announced last October that it was reorganising its music businesses in order to tackle sluggish market conditions.

"This will be a challenging year for PolyGram's music division, particularly in the US where market instability is likely to persist for the next six to 12 months," PolyGram president and CEO Alain Levy said in a statement.

"Nevertheless, we remain optimistic that our continued success in breaking new talent and the measures we have taken to adapt to changing markets around the world will create the right conditions for longterm growth," he added.
PolyGram's expanding film unit moved into profit in the second half of last year. The company left its dividend unchanged at 0.95 guilders per share. ($1=1.857 Guilder)
